subject: Not able to use specified number of cores

messages.author: b940bb03851c507a
messages.subject: Not able to use specified number of cores
parts:
To all,

I'm trying to run userGWAS using 16 cores, but it keeps using 1 less than all the cores available. Does anyone have an idea?

Best regards,

Austin

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: Not able to use specified number of cores
parts:
Hi Austin, 

The default is for the package to use 1 less cores than are available in the computing environment. If you want to use all cores then you should set the cores argument to 16 (i.e., cores=16). 

Best, 
  Andrew

messages.author: 8c4d003b861b01f7
messages.subject: Re: Not able to use specified number of cores
parts:
Hi Austin,

I know this is an older thread, I'm just leaving this here for future reference, in case other users end up looking for a solution to this here.
Setting the cores argument to the number of cores your system has is not recommended and will likely make it perform worse. You will want to keep (at least) one core free for the main R thread, as well as your OS processes. On a clean Linux server you can probably get away with leaving 1 core for those, but on a Windows machine or your personal Mac or Linux I would recommend leaving at least two cores free for the main R thread and OS stuff. If you set it to the exact number of cores all these processes will start competing for resources which can dramatically slow things down as the data for each process has to be swapped back and forth, and scheduling processes will start to use more resources to figure out which process gets how many resources and when.

Best,
Matthijs
